overlooked_assumption: The agent assumed that the presence of `all-team-models` in a key's model list unconditionally meant the key should have unrestricted model access, without considering whether the key actually belongs to a team. It failed to add a `team_id is not None` guard before skipping the model check.
why_it_breaks: When a teamless key (team_id is None) has `all-team-models` in its models list, the unconditional `elif "all-team-models" in valid_token.models: pass` skips the key-level model access check entirely. This allows the key to call any model despite having no team, which is the auth bypass. The fix adds `and valid_token.team_id is not None` so that only team-owned keys with `all-team-models` skip the check; teamless keys fall through to `can_key_call_model`, which correctly denies access because the sentinel model cannot be resolved to a real model.

evidence.quote: However, two call-path functions still unconditionally skip key-level model checks when `all-team-models` is present, without checking whether the key actually belongs to a team:

1. `_enforce_key_and_fallback_model_access` (the main auth entry point for `/chat/completions` etc.) had `elif "all-team-models" in valid_token.models: pass` - skipping the model check entirely regardless of team membership
